## Seeding the out-of-scope reading, and the order to read it in

*2026-09-25 20:42:31 · curation*

The seed entry of this afternoon left three questions open, and the owner
answered all three: **file all of it**, including the works that are not
papers; **seed from abstracts and skims**, then triage the result, because
the deeper readings still have to happen; and **when in doubt, the
anthology**. This entry records what the seeding did and the order the deeper
readings should take.

**29 works filed here, 5 to the anthology. 26 carry a `Skimmed` NOTE, 3 carry
none. Every LIT is `Deferred` ("Unreviewed"), with a status note saying it was
seeded and not read in full.**

## How it was done, and how far to trust it

Four agents each fetched one cluster's sources and wrote a dossier per work:
the bibliography, a paraphrased abstract, skim bullets each naming the
section or page it came from, what a deeper reading should check, a priority,
and what could and could not be reached. A script turned each dossier into a
LIT and, where the work was actually skimmed, a NOTE. The LIT's "Standing in
the record" keeps the priority, the checks and the access record, so the
triage below can be audited from the documents rather than from this entry.

**Depth was downgraded where the skim was not a skim.** The concussion review
(`LIT-029`) and Bourrat on individuality (`LIT-005`) were reached
only through a fetch tool that returns a model-written summary; the
publishers served a bot check. A summary of the text is not a skim of it, so
both are filed at abstract depth, with no NOTE. So is the wasp-venom
proteomics paper (`LIT-026`), where only the abstract was reachable.

**Identities corrected on the way.** The network-dimension paper the triage
called *Unveiling the Dimensionality of Networks of Networks* is filed under
the title it took in v2 and in *Phys. Rev. E* 114, L022301. The arXiv hash
`quant-ph/9601020` is Fuchs's 1995 PhD thesis. The two unnamed PDFs are
Bottke et al. on the Eulalia impact shower and Rungsa et al. 2016 in
*Toxicon*. The hearing transcript (`LIT-012`) matches the CourtListener
docket for D. Minn. 0:26-cv-00603 by case number and judge; the Drive copy
has not been checked against a docket entry, a transcript holds no ruling,
and whether a written order followed is unverified.

**The seven that are not papers.** The ISW report, JP 3-12, Drezner's essay
and Gelman's post carry `url:` sources. The three court documents carry
descriptive titles marked `[descriptive title]`, because a filing has a
caption, not a title.

## The five that went to the anthology

The seed named four boundary cases, and the owner's rule sent all four there.
A fifth joined them: *Rigor with Machine Learning from Field Theory to the
Poincaré Conjecture*, triaged under "other sciences", whose transferable
claim is methodological — let a learned model search and an exact procedure
verify what it finds. That is an `analysis-and-evaluation` claim, so it is in
doubt, so it is the anthology's. *Topos and Stacks* went under
`model-architecture` and `concept-geometry` rather than the
`analysis-and-evaluation` the seed guessed: it is about what an architecture
lets information and semantics do, not about how to measure anything.

That leaves `neuroscience` with no work under it as the primary topic, only
as the concussion review's second tag. The word stays; it was blurbed for a
cluster the reading feed keeps producing.

## Reading time is not the priority here, and why

The two largest totals in the whole feed are the Eulalia paper (11,500 s) and
the network-dimension letter (6,080 s), and their dossiers rank them low and
medium. That is not a contradiction: time measures the owner's attention, and
the priority below measures what a close reading would add to this record.

*Corrected the same evening.* This section first said the long totals meant
those works had "probably been read", and that a deeper-reading pass should
begin by asking the owner which NOTEs to mark `Read`. That misreads the
status. A NOTE records a reading *this record* made — `Read` is "the full
text, closely enough to state its assumptions and results exactly" — and it
is earned by doing that reading, not by the owner's attention in a browser
tab. The owner's reply: the status is an invitation to read the thing. So the
deeper readings below are this record's to perform, in this order, and a
`Skimmed` NOTE is replaced by a `Read` one when the reading is done.

## The order for deeper readings

**First — read in full.** Short, foundational, and each unlocks others.

1. **Spekkens, *Quasi-quantization*** (`LIT-007`, 1,615 s). The framing
   for the two later Spekkens-group papers. Read it before *Why interference
   phenomena…* (`LIT-019`) and the structure theorem (`LIT-003`),
   whose skims are enough once this is in hand. §II–III, the technical core,
   is what the skim missed.
2. **Abramsky & Brandenburger, the sheaf-theoretic structure of non-locality**
   (`LIT-016`). The core theorems are short. *Corrected by the reading
   ([NOTE-016](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-016.md)):* this entry first called it "this record's one bridge to the
   anthology", with *Topos and Stacks* building on it and sheaf neural
   networks descending from it. Neither holds. Belfiore & Bennequin cite it
   once, in a related-work list, and use nothing from it; the sheaf-network
   papers checked do not cite it. It is first on its own merits, as the
   founding and fully proved paper of its programme.
3. **The *U.S. v. Google* remedies opinion** (`LIT-006`, 1,040 s over
   four sessions). The skim did not reach the findings of fact on generative
   AI (pp. 17–46 — the entry first said 17–36): how a federal court understood LLMs, grounding and the GenAI
   market. That is the part worth reading.
4. **Mediano et al. and Varley & Hoel, side by side** (`LIT-025`,
   `LIT-027`, ~2,500 s combined). Two definitions of emergence from the
   same theme issue. A deeper reading is a comparison, and it should take in
   Rosas et al. 2020, the primary behind the first. Neither is the anthology's
   `capability-thresholds` sense of "emergence", and whoever reads them should
   write that down.

**Second — targeted sections, not the whole work.**

- Forman–Ricci curvature (`LIT-020`): the curvature formula and flow
  definitions, §2.3 and §4.
- Fuchs's thesis (`LIT-018`): chapters 2–3.
- Nested HDP (`LIT-002`): the SVI derivation in §4.
- The network-dimension letter (`LIT-028`): the Supplementary Material
  derivation, after asking whether it was already read.
- JP 3-12 (`LIT-015`): the definitions and the authorities chapter.
- The Rhode Island Hospital subpoena order (`LIT-024`): whether it was
  appealed, and how it interacts with the Texas enforcement order.
- Lindgren & Liukkonen (`LIT-001`): the linearization assumptions,
  against Nelson's stochastic mechanics.

**Third — the skim is enough unless an interest makes it otherwise.** The
remaining sixteen: Eulalia, wasp venom, vehicle routing, the emergence
theme-issue introduction, Betti Lagrangians, spectral sets, Ricci-flow
community detection, quantum thermodynamics, Pitman–Yor topic models, the two
Spekkens-group follow-ups named above, the concussion review, Bourrat, the ISW
report, the hearing transcript, Drezner and Gelman. Several of their
dossiers say the same thing: the value is in the primary sources the piece
cites, not in a second pass over the piece.

None of this promotes anything. A work leaves `Deferred` when somebody has
read it closely, and here nobody has yet.

## The first five close readings, and what the seed got wrong

*2026-09-25 21:30:54 · curation*

The first tier of the reading order in `2026/09/25/204231` is done. The owner's
correction set this pass in motion: `Read` is not a question for the owner
about their browser history. It is a status the record earns by reading the
work, and it is an invitation to do that. Five works were read in full, each by
one reader working from the full text and the seeded skim. Each skim NOTE
became a `Read` NOTE, at version 2, with a claims table and a section listing
what the full text contradicted. All five LITs left `Deferred` and are now
`Active`.

| LIT | NOTE | work | what the reading changed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LIT-007` | `NOTE-013` | Spekkens, *Quasi-quantization* | The continuous-variable equivalence is with the *quadrature* subtheory, which sits strictly inside the Gaussian one, and not with "stabilizer/Gaussian". Table II's list of classically explainable phenomena is asserted, not derived. |
| `LIT-016` | `NOTE-016` | Abramsky & Brandenburger | The paper is **not a bridge** to the machine-learning work. The seed and this record's reading order both said it was. |
| `LIT-006` | `NOTE-004` | *U.S. v. Google* remedies opinion | The data remedy is far narrower than the skim said. The GenAI findings run to p. 46. The opinion holds the *opposite* of "search data is a moat for LLMs" (p. 156). |
| `LIT-025` | `NOTE-010` | Mediano et al., *Greater than the parts* | It is a restatement of Rosas et al. 2020 with no new theorem. The summary had inherited the review's overstatement that it "extends" that paper. |
| `LIT-027` | `NOTE-020` | Varley & Hoel, *Emergence as the conversion of information* | The headline conversion **reverses** for redundancy-leaning deterministic systems, and the Gaussian effect is 0.005–0.07. There are internal errors: a swapped figure caption, and a reference to a figure that does not exist. |

## The pattern

Every one of the five skims carried at least one claim the full text does not
support. Every one of those errors made the paper look **more connected, more
general or more conclusive** than it is. That is the drift the anthology's
`DP-010` warns about: the most citable sentence is often the least supported.
It also held on this record's own most-cited sentence. This record called
Abramsky & Brandenburger "this record's one bridge to the anthology", with
*Topos and Stacks* building on it and sheaf neural networks descending from it.
Belfiore & Bennequin cite it once, in a related-work list, and use nothing from
it. The two sheaf-network papers checked do not cite it at all. The claim was
corrected in place, in this record's reading order and in the anthology's
boundary entry, and each correction is marked as one.

The lesson for the seeding step is simple. A skim is honest about its depth,
but it is not honest about **connections**. A connection named from a skim is a
guess, and it should be written as one.

## What the reading turned up to file

**Rosas et al. 2020, *Reconciling emergences*** (*PLoS Comput. Biol.*), is the
primary source behind `LIT-025`. The review restates its theorem, and every
proof and assumption lives there. It is not held. It is the next filing in this
cluster, and `LIT-025` cannot be cited for the theorem until it is.

## Every work read but two, and what the readings did to the seed

*2026-09-25 22:10:08 · curation*

The reading order of `2026/09/25/204231` is done. **27 of the 29 works now
have a `Read` NOTE.** Each is written from the full text, with a claims table
and a section listing what the reading contradicted in the seed. The two left
over are the Toxicon venom proteomics paper (`LIT-026`) and the concussion
review (`LIT-029`). Neither is open access. Every route to a full text failed:
PMC and Europe PMC, the publishers, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and
ResearchGate. Both stay `Deferred` at abstract depth. Reading either needs a
PDF supplied by hand.

## Where the readings placed the works

| standing | count | works |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `Active` | 22 | the rest |
| `Proposed` | 3 | Bourrat (`LIT-005`), the Eulalia impact shower (`LIT-009`), Spectral Networks (`LIT-017`) |
| `Rejected` | 1 | Lindgren & Liukkonen (`LIT-001`) |
| `Deferred` | 2 | the two unobtainable works |

**Bourrat.** The measure it proposes is never computed on any system. Its
claim that the measure equals the observational one fails on a two-bit
counterexample: take S′ = S ⊕ E with uniform inputs. Then A = 1 bit, and the
interventional measure is 0.

**The Eulalia paper.** It is a plausibility model. Every lunar date scales
from one sample-dated crater. Its five fitted breakup ages span 785–965 Myr,
not the 800–900 its prose says.

**Spectral Networks.** It is unrefereed, and several theorem statements are
broader than their proofs.

**Lindgren & Liukkonen.** It puts the imaginary unit in twice by hand:
through √g instead of √(−g), and through a complex noise variance chosen to
force linearity.

## The pattern, held across all 27

Every skim carried at least one claim that the full text does not support.
Every one of those errors pointed in the same direction: toward the work being
more connected, more general or more conclusive than it is. The first five
readings (`2026/09/25/213054`) found this. Twenty-two more did not break it.
The corrections include:

- **Theorems stated more broadly than proved.** Ni et al.'s Theorem 4.1.
  Casals & Nho's Theorem 3.
- **Printed equations that do not do what the text says.**
  - Paisley et al.'s SVI update re-adds the prior at every step.
  - Weber et al.'s workflow silently uses the flow form the paper had just
    rejected.
  - Grimaldi et al.'s finite-size prefactors have the wrong power of N. A
    numerical check confirmed this.
- **Headline numbers the paper's own tables contradict.**
  - The Eulalia age range.
  - The waste-routing GA's "consistently" better routes.
  - The ~30% optimality gaps the skim left out.
- **Attributions that were syntheses.** The "Russian military definition" in
  the ISW report is Clark's composite, not a quotation.

Several readers also did their own arithmetic, and those checks are part of
the record:

- a comb-network simulation;
- a linear-programming check of a lemma;
- a Kesten–Stigum detectability calculation, which puts the stochastic
  block model's limit near 0.78, where Ni et al. read collapse as absence;
- ontic-state counts for the structure theorem, which match the GPT
  dimension exactly.

Where a reader went beyond the paper, its NOTE says so.

## Filing questions the readings raised

- **Rosas et al. 2020** is still the primary source behind `LIT-025`, and it is
  not held.
- **Levitsky & Way, *The Path to American Authoritarianism*** (Foreign Affairs,
  Feb 2025) is the primary source for most of Drezner's post (`LIT-022`), and

- **JP 3-12** has a December 2022 revision. Secondary reports say it is

- **The Rhode Island order (`LIT-024`)** is on appeal in the First Circuit,
  with argument on 2026-10-07. The Texas enforcement order is on appeal in the

## First: read in full, in these pairs

1. **Bourrat's coarse-graining account of individuality ([LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)),
   alongside his *Adding causality…* ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), already read).** It is the same

## The papers-feed swept for philosophy: 119 works seeded

*2026-09-26 05:58:20 · curation · record*

The owner asked for the papers-feed tracker's snapshot to be checked for more
philosophy to file, after Nagel ([LIT-096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md)). The owner also decided
that everything from the sweep stays here, and asked for anthology candidates
to be flagged with a tag. That tag is `anthology-candidate`, from
[ADR-005](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-005.md).

## The funnel

| stage | count |
| --- | ---: |
| papers in the snapshot (`gh-store-snapshot.json`) | 7,800 |
| scored as possibly philosophy | 217 |
| kept by hand, with duplicate captures merged | 132 |
| already held (the SEP entry on structural realism) | 1 |
| seed dossiers written, by six agents | 131 |
| dropped as not philosophy | 3 |
| merged as the same work under another capture | 9 |
| **filed, all `Deferred`** | **119** |

95 were skimmed from a full text and carry a `Skimmed` NOTE. 24 are seeded from
the abstract alone.

**How the score worked:**

- **Journal names:** *Synthese*, *Mind*, *Philosophy Compass*, *Biology &
  Philosophy*, *Minds and Machines* and the like.
- **Source URLs:** PhilPapers, PhilArchive, PhilSci-Archive, the SEP and JSTOR.
- **Keywords:** philosophy words in the title and the first 1,500 characters of
  the abstract.

*Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society* matches the journal filter
and is a science journal. Its hits were removed by hand.

**The score misses philosophy that carries no signal:** an arXiv paper in a
physics category, say, that never uses a philosophy word. A second pass over
the low scorers would find more. Nobody has made that pass.

**Three drops:**

- a political-science paper on propaganda technologies;
- a mathematics manuscript on Connes' rigidity conjecture, hiding behind an
  unresolved PhilPapers code;
- a JSTOR chapter on Hero of Alexandria's automata.

## Traps

- **PhilPapers, PhilArchive and Taylor & Francis are behind Cloudflare** from
  here. The tracker had captured about twenty of them as "Just a moment..." or
  as a bare hash, with no title.
  - The agents identified them from the PhilPapers code (an author-surname +
    title stem) and web search.
  - They read the texts through Wayback copies (`web.archive.org/web/2026id_/…`),
    author pages, PhilSci-Archive with a plain `curl` user agent, and
    `rd.springer.com`.
- **Duplicates only show once titles are resolved.** Seven of the nine merges
  were an unresolved PhilPapers capture of a work already in the batch under
  its journal URL: Wallace, Vetter, Floridi, Drayson, Šekrst, the
  distributional-semantics chapter, and the epistemic-injustice paper. So
  deduplicate *after* the seed, by DOI, arXiv id and title, never only before
  it. Reading time is pooled across the captures.
- **The dossiers cross-referenced each other by batch id** (`p078`). The filing
  script copied those into 150 files as-is. They were rewritten to the record's
  codes before commit.

## The vocabulary

Two words were added by [ADR-006](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-006.md):

- **`epistemology`**, used by fourteen works. One had no topic at all, and
  the rest had the nearest wrong one.
- **`logic`**, used by two.

A `philosophy-of-mind` word was considered and not added. The mental-causation
papers are honestly `metaphysics`.

**Two works are flagged `anthology-candidate`:**

- *Borges and AI* (Bottou & Schölkopf);
- Terziyan et al., on ethics carried across generations of AI.

The borderline cases the dossiers kept here are:

- the three philosophy-of-unsupervised-learning papers;
- Mallory's *LLMs Are Stochastic Measuring Devices*.

## A pass over the mereology tag: four readings, eight retags

*2026-09-26 06:37:03 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a pass over the `mereology` tag. It held six works: two
read and four skimmed seeds from the morning's philosophy sweep. All four
seeds were read in full, and each is now `Active`:

| work | what the reading found |
| --- | --- |
| Varzi, SEP *Mereology* ([LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md)) | the formal reference: M ⊂ MM ⊂ EM ⊂ GEM, with the exact axioms. GEM is reached from M by exactly three pairings of a supplementation principle and a sum principle. |
| Carroll, *Reality as a Vector in Hilbert Space* ([LIT-123](../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md)) | a programme, not a result: parts are factorisations chosen afterwards, to suit the dynamics |
| Register, *The Depth of the Body* ([LIT-138](../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md)) | a moral "body part" relation, bounded below by depth, applied to BCIs hosted in the cloud |
| Meincke, *One or two?* ([LIT-142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md)) | process ontology keeps the foster as a part, and makes the count indeterminate |

## What the readings corrected

Each skim overstated its paper, in the same direction: a proposal was reported
as a result.

- **The SEP entry** was summarised as calling the partial-order core
  "uncontroversial". §2.1 says the opposite: all three core axioms have serious
  dissenters, and Antisymmetry "can hardly be regarded as constitutive".
- **Carroll** was credited with a uniqueness result for the quasi-classical
  factorisation. He does not claim one. The only uniqueness claim is for local
  factorisations, and it is borrowed from Cotler et al. Carroll's own criterion
  needs inputs beyond the spectrum, which he admits are "somewhat cheating".
  Fields were reported as "recovered". The essay only hopes to recover them.
- **Carroll's finiteness figure, e^(e^123),** is what the paper prints (p. 5).
  It does not follow from the paper's own premise, S = πr²/G, which gives a
  single exponential. Quote the order of magnitude, never the figure.
- **Register** was summarised as resting his ethics on the real-definition
  metaphysics and dissolving the ownership conflict. He says the principles do
  not depend on that ontology, and the conflict is narrowed, not dissolved.
- **Meincke** was summarised as offering a rival to the Parthood View. She keeps
  parthood and rejects only its pairing with substance ontology.

## Eight works that were about parts and wholes and did not say so

The tag's blurb reads "parts and wholes — composition, individuation of
systems and collectives". The test was whether someone browsing that topic
would expect the work. Eight held works pass, and now carry the tag after their
existing topics:

- **Composition of wholes:** [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) (ΦID causal emergence) and [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md)
  (emergence as the conversion of information).
- **Constitution:** [LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md) (*The Extended Mind*).
- **Individuation:**
  - [LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md) (Bourrat, reproducees and reproducers)
  - [LIT-167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md) (Baedke, *The Organism*)
  - [LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md) (SEP, *Biological Individuals*)
  - [LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md) (Griesemer & Shavit, scaffolding individuality)
- **A collective as a candidate subject:** [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) (Schwitzgebel, the United
  States as conscious).

Considered and not tagged: *Philosophy of Microbiology*, collective
intelligence and the ant/human puzzle study. They discuss collectives, but not
as a question about parts and wholes.

## The tag is wider than its reference

The SEP entry excludes two senses of "mereology":

- the systems-theory and ecological sense (its note 1);
- quantum part–whole formalisms (its note 18).

The tag's blurb names both on purpose: "individuation of systems and
collectives". So [LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md) is the background for the philosophical works on the
tag ([LIT-142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md), [LIT-138](../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md) and the individuality cluster). It is only loosely the
background for [LIT-123](../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md), [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) and [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), which use "part" for a tensor
factor or a coarse-grained variable. A reader should not expect the SEP's
axioms to hold of those.

## Still open on the tag

- **The two Bourrat papers** ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)) remain `Proposed`. Each would
  be settled by a worked model: an explicit computation of its individuality
  measure on a model of an evolutionary transition. Another reading cannot
  supply that.
- **Six of the newly tagged works are still `Deferred`:** the four
  individuality works, *The Extended Mind* and Schwitzgebel. They are the
  natural next readings for this tag.

## What the readings corrected

The skims overstated in the same direction as the first pass found: a proposal
was reported as a result, or a sufficient condition as a list of paradigm
features.

- **Clark & Chalmers' conditions** on a coupled resource were summarised as
  sufficient ("provided…"). The paper says it gives no "categorical answers".
- **Schwitzgebel's §6** does not test the Dretske, Dennett, Humphrey and Tononi
  theories. It rebuts four objections, Chalmers's the most seriously.
- **Bourrat's dossier** had reproductive causal control evolving through
  scaffolding. The paper (p. 21) says scaffolded collectives get control for
  free, and that what must evolve is autonomy.
- **The SEP entry's framework** was credited to Pepper & Herron, who only pose
  the question.

## Where the works disagree

- **Genes.** Bourrat ([LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md)) makes genes, like hearts, mere reproducees. The
  SEP entry ([LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md)) places genes as Darwinian individuals. The record holds
  both. Neither is retired.
- **Bourrat against his own earlier papers** ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)):
  - *Inherited:* nothing is computed; the environment is handled by
    conditioning; and the control measure is biased toward fine grains.
  - *Fixed:* autonomy (associational) and control (interventional) are kept
    apart.
  - *Scale rule:* "smallest object at maximal MI" runs opposite to [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)'s
    coarsest grain.

## A defect found and fixed along the way

The script that writes a Read NOTE rewrites the LIT's summary. It kept a
citation head only when the head ended in ")." or ">.". For "Clark et al.
(1998), DOI-10.1093/analys/58.1.7." it fell back to splitting at the first
". ", and kept only "Clark et al.". That dropped the year and the identifier.

- **Two of this pass's summaries** ([LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), [LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)) were hit.
- **Eight summaries from earlier readings** were hit too: [LIT-001](../../record/literature.d/LIT-001.md), [LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md),
  [LIT-035](../../record/literature.d/LIT-035.md), [LIT-053](../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md), [LIT-069](../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), [LIT-080](../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md), [LIT-087](../../record/literature.d/LIT-087.md) and [LIT-094](../../record/literature.d/LIT-094.md).

All ten were restored from each document's own fields. The script now matches
"Author (YEAR), identifier." first.

- **Check that finds it:** any summary whose first lines carry no "(YYYY"
  lost its head.
- **Left alone:** [LIT-074](../../record/literature.d/LIT-074.md), whose unverified head is deliberate.

## What the pass established

- **Birch and Seth answer each other.** Birch's v4 names Seth, and its §12
  overlaps his BBS commentary on Seth. They disagree on four things:
  - whether the illusion that an AI is conscious can be blocked at the level
    of belief (Birch: yes; Seth: perhaps not, like Müller-Lyer);
  - how likely consciousness is in current LLMs;
  - whether a link between consciousness and life is testable;
  - what a global workspace found in an LLM would show.

  They agree on Nagel's definition ([LIT-096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md)) and on treating LLMs as
  role-players.
- **Schwitzgebel's arguments are layered.** *The Weirdness of the World*
  collects the earlier arguments. [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) is its chapter 2 in manuscript and
  chapter 3 in print, revised: the IIT footnote is much expanded and now
  engages the expander-graph case that [LIT-185](../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md) defends against. *AI and
  Consciousness* ([LIT-191](../../record/literature.d/LIT-191.md)) continues its chapters 10 and 11. [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) now says so.
- **Kleiner & Ludwig's published version drops a result.** The finding that
  metric spaces are not structures of experience is only in arXiv v1 §4.
  Cite the preprint for it.
- **Veit now rejects plant consciousness.** That conflicts with the paper he
  co-wrote, [LIT-193](../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md).

<a id="20260926202345"></a>

## Ladyman and Ross on the record: ontic structural realism and rainforest realism

*2026-09-26 20:23:45 · curation · record*

The owner asked for James Ladyman and Don Ross's accounts of **ontic
structural realism (OSR)** and **rainforest realism** to be on the record,
ideally from their book *Every Thing Must Go: Metaphysics Naturalized* (OUP
2007, with Spurrett and Collier).

## What could not be obtained

Only legitimate sources were used: publishers, repositories, the authors' own
pages and the Wayback Machine. Shadow libraries were ruled out.

- ***Every Thing Must Go*.** Not open access, and OUP returned 403. No free
  sample was found. An archive.org upload labelled "Public Domain" is an
  unauthorised copy and was not used.
- **Ladyman 1998, "What is structural realism?"** (SHPS), the founding OSR
  paper. Paywalled, with no repository copy.
- **Ross 2000, "Rainforest Realism: a Dennettian theory of existence"** (in
  *Dennett's Philosophy*, MIT). Closed access.
- **Berenstain & Ladyman 2012, "Ontic Structural Realism and Modality".**
  On PhilArchive, which blocked this session, as did the Wayback Machine.

## What was read instead

Four freely available works, each read in full and `Active`:

| work | what it contributes |
| --- | --- |
| Ladyman 2001, *Science, Metaphysics and Structural Realism* ([LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md)) | the earliest free statement of OSR by its founder |
| Ladyman, *Patterns All the Way Up* (2024 preprint, MIT 2026) ([LIT-219](../../record/literature.d/LIT-219.md)) | the core of rainforest realism, and his current second thoughts |
| Ross 2008, *Ontic Structural Realism and Economics* ([LIT-218](../../record/literature.d/LIT-218.md)) | OSR carried beyond physics |
| Dennett 1991, *Real Patterns* ([LIT-220](../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md)) | the criterion that rainforest realism generalises. Read because Ross 2000 was unreachable. |

**What each supplies:**

- **Ladyman 2001:**
  - the quantum non-individuality argument, framed as an underdetermination
    between individuals and non-individuals, not a proof;
  - entanglement against Humean supervenience;
  - theories describing "the modal structure of the phenomena";
  - a non-eliminative line: "the phenomena have structure but they are not
    structure".
- ***Patterns All the Way Up*:**
  - "to be is to be a real pattern";
  - scale-relative, effective ontology;
  - no single hierarchy of levels;
  - agnosticism, not denial, about a fundamental level (fn. 9);
  - the Principle of Naturalistic Closure quoted from the book (p. 37), then
    called "problematic" by Ladyman himself.
- **Ross 2008:** individuals are "book-keeping devices", not denied. That is a
  deflationary third position, which Chakravartty's dilemma ([LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md)) does not
  address.
- **Dennett 1991:** a pattern is real iff some description beats the bit map,
  "whether or not anyone can concoct it". Rival real patterns can coexist.

## How far the two ideas are covered

- **OSR:** covered by the new works together with [LIT-045](../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md) (the SEP entry, by
  Ladyman) and [LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md). The explicit eliminative/non-eliminative choice still
  rests on those two held notes: no new text by the authors stakes it out.
- **Rainforest realism:** covered for real patterns, scale relativity, the
  rejection of a fundamental level of individuals, and the PNC.

**Gaps:**

- The **Primacy of Physics Constraint** is stated in none of the four.
- The **book's own real-patterns definition** (Ross 2000 and *Every Thing
  Must Go*), which adds projectibility to Dennett's compression, is referred
  to but not quoted.

The book, Ross 2000, or Berenstain & Ladyman would close both. Berenstain &
Ladyman is the one to try first, from a session that can reach PhilArchive.

## Corrections the readings raise

These are recorded here, not written into the older notes, because each is
about what the *new* sources say.

- **[NOTE-038](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md) and [NOTE-129](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-129.md)** credit the projectibility and perspective clauses
  to "real patterns" in general. Dennett's own criterion is plain lossless
  compression.
- **[NOTE-129](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-129.md) has Ladyman and Ross "deny" a fundamental level.** *Patterns All
  the Way Up* fn. 9 says they are agnostic about one. That may be a later
  retreat, or a misreading; the book would settle which.
- **The record's two accounts of real patterns disagree** on whether the
  fundamental level is itself a pattern: Wallace ([LIT-151](../../record/literature.d/LIT-151.md)) against Ladyman &
  Lorenzetti ([LIT-184](../../record/literature.d/LIT-184.md)). *Patterns All the Way Up* states the disagreement.

| nLab, *Yoneda lemma* ([LIT-221](../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md)) | the lemma stated and proved, with the embedding as fully faithful and the corollary y(c) ≅ y(d) ⇔ c ≅ d, in a self-contained unit that can be read whole |
| Bain 2013, *Category-theoretic structure and radical ontic structural realism* ([LIT-223](../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md)) | the main category-theoretic argument for *radical* (eliminative) OSR |
| Lam & Wüthrich 2015, *No categorial support for radical ontic structural realism* ([LIT-222](../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md)) | the reply. It `corrects` Bain in the record's relation graph. |

## The finding: no source in the core literature names Yoneda

Neither Bain nor Lam & Wüthrich mentions the Yoneda lemma, representable
functors or universal properties. Lal & Teh (arXiv:1404.3049), searched in
full text, does not either. Eva 2016 (EJPS) could not be obtained from a
legitimate free source.

- **Bain stops one step short.** He quotes Awodey on objects "determined …
  by their position in a structure", and defines products by probing them
  from outside, but never takes the step to the lemma.
- **Lam & Wüthrich use two of its consequences without the name.**
  Generalised elements X → A exist in every category, and morphisms "only
  distinguish isomorphism classes of structures".

Two works that do name the lemma were found and **not filed**:

- **Adlam 2025 (arXiv:2507.20313).** One sentence: Yoneda "implies that
  objects may emerge from the 'morphisms'". The source it cites, Yokura 2017,
  was read in full and says nothing of the kind.
- **Hendren, Grasso, Ellia & Tononi 2026 (arXiv:2608.24928).** A box calls
  Yoneda OSR's "mathematical centerpiece". That is an assertion, and the paper
  is about qualia, not physics.

## What the lemma does and does not support

The lemma says an object is determined **up to isomorphism** by its hom-functor,
its relations to every other object. That supports **objects as positions in a
structure**: the non-eliminative OSR of Ladyman 2001 ([LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md)), and Lam &
Wüthrich's "balanced" OSR. It does **not** support radical OSR, for three
reasons:

1. **The determination presupposes the category's objects.** The hom-functor
   is indexed by them, and the conclusion is an isomorphism between two of
   them.
2. **It needs the composition structure, not merely which hom-sets exist.**
   The nLab page's own counterexample has two non-isomorphic objects whose
   hom-sets are in bijection at every object.
3. **It fixes objects only up to isomorphism.** That is the categorical twin
   of the limit on weak discernibility in Leitgeb & Ladyman ([LIT-154](../../record/literature.d/LIT-154.md)).

So Bain's inference to eliminating objects is overstated. His reliance on
elements as arrows out of a terminal object also fails once generalised
elements are admitted.

## Errors the readings found in the works

- **nLab:** its finite counterexample breaks the identity law as written, and
  its HoTT proof has small errors. It gives only the presheaf form.
  Nat(Hom(A,−),F) ≅ F(A) follows by passing to C^op.
- **Bain:** treats sections of a sheaf of Einstein algebras as maximal ideals,
  and mis-defines a maximal ideal.
- **Both papers:** say Hilb has no products. Direct sums are products.
- **Lam & Wüthrich:** mis-define a topos, and say non-commutative algebras
  have no maximal ideals.

normative conclusion. Its tags are now `social-science` and `cognition`. The
reader suggested `religion` too, but the paper mentions religion only in
passing, so it was not added.

## The readings

Four works were read in full, and all are `Active`:

- [LIT-098](../../record/literature.d/LIT-098.md), Veit, on health concepts and social justice. Read from the
  PhilSci-Archive preprint; the journal version sat behind a bot challenge.
- [LIT-101](../../record/literature.d/LIT-101.md), the moral-disciplining paper. Read from the accepted manuscript on
  OSF.
- [LIT-179](../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md), Schmauder et al., *Algorithmic Nudging*.
- [LIT-198](../../record/literature.d/LIT-198.md), Hooker's SEP entry *Rule Consequentialism*.

The corrections, as in the epistemology pass, mostly took claims away from the
seeds:

- **Veit.** The skim had him "conceding" that Kukla can hold the institution
  of medicine fixed. That is the second horn of his own dilemma: holding
  medicine fixed makes the account normativist "in name only".
- **Schmauder et al.** The seed said AI systems "can learn nudges that exploit
  biases nobody has documented". Both case studies exploit documented biases.
  The undocumented case is a conjecture.
- **Hooker.** The seed had the view survive by "acceptance by less than
  everyone and a prevent-disaster rule". That misassigns the replies. Ranking
  rules by the expected good of teaching and accepting them answers the
  collapse objection. The prevent-disaster rule answers only rule-worship. The
  90% threshold is there for punishment rules.

  passing, but their machinery is prediction, not information.
- **[LIT-136](../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md)** (Floridi on personal identity). It is philosophy of information
  in name: its tool is levels of abstraction, not entropy or channels.
- **[LIT-044](../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md)** (Stigler on maximum likelihood). Fisher information appears
  there as history of statistics, which `probabilistic-modeling` already
  covers.

## One relation

Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski argue that Vera et al.'s bound on I(X;U) is
vacuous in realistic settings. It is recorded as `corrects`. The claim comes
from a skim, and a reading should confirm it.

## "Do we even need Riesz?"

The owner's note under the Riesz heading asked this. The dossier agent's
answer, from reading the four pages: **yes, as a lemma, not as a reading.**

- Riesz is what makes kernels exist. Evaluation at a point is a continuous
  functional, and Riesz turns it into the kernel vector k_x.
- It is why a linear probe or "concept direction" can be treated as a vector.
- It is why adjoints, and so the spectral arguments in the self-supervised
  learning papers, make sense.
- Adler's REU paper ends on Radon–Nikodym, the density result that KL
  divergence and mutual information, and so the bottlenecks, rest on.
- Bra–ket is notation.
- GNS is a suggestive analogy: a state determines its representation up to
  unitary equivalence. That echoes the Platonic hypothesis's kernel
  comparisons, but no representation-learning paper found uses it.

None of the four pages makes these connections itself. They are the dossier's
own and are marked as such.
